text: AWS Amplify, Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS
How the cloud services support a student task and study management system
Cloud Computing  |  Shah & Anchor Kutchhi Engineering College
A web application for students to plan academic work and monitor progress
Create, edit and complete personal tasks
Filter by subject, priority, status and due date
View dashboard totals and upcoming work
TaskFlow separates the browser interface, API processing and database records. Each layer has a clear responsibility in the planned AWS deployment.
The report describes a cloud-ready design. It does not claim a live AWS deployment.
A managed service for building and hosting web applications
Amplify can host a static web frontend, connect deployments to a source repository, and provide a public HTTPS address for the application.
Serve the web app over HTTPS
TaskFlow uses Amplify as the planned home for the React and Vite frontend.
No server setup for the UI
Virtual servers that run application software in AWS
EC2 provides compute capacity. Teams choose an instance, install the required software and run the application process on the server.
The planned EC2 instance hosts the Flask REST API.
The browser sends an authenticated API request.
Flask validates JWT identity and applies task rules.
The API returns JSON for the React interface.
The API also controls access to private tasks and study-file actions.
RDS provides managed database instances. For TaskFlow, PostgreSQL is the planned production database while SQLite supports local development.
PostgreSQL on RDS stores the data that the API needs for each student.

title, subject, priority
status, due date

file metadata
owner and task link
Each API query uses the authenticated user identity to scope private records.
Example: a student creates a task from the browser.
Amplify hosts the React frontend where this workflow begins.
TaskFlow Cloud maps each service to a specific layer.
The report documents this AWS architecture as cloud-ready. Local testing used the React, Flask and SQLite development setup.
